rows.verified: Fairground controllers must plan, manage and monitor erection, operation and dismantling so workers and the public are not exposed to uncontrolled risks.
Ride staff must receive enough information and training to operate safely and protect themselves and others.
Fairground rides require annual inspection by a competent person and should not operate with a gap in the required test.
Ride maintenance and safety-critical repairs must be performed and reviewed by competent people.
Controllers must have systems for foreseeable emergencies and safe evacuation without relying solely on emergency services.
Fair organisers must manage the whole site, ride layout, public movement and availability of trained emergency personnel.
Operators must enforce applicable rider restrictions and maintain restraints and other protective measures.
Rides should be designed, reviewed, inspected, maintained and operated safely, with exclusion zones and restrictions respected.
Fairground controls depend on device design, maturity, inspection, maintenance, setup, weather, rider characteristics, operator competence and emergency capability.
Fairground evidence is device-, operator-, site- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level ride-injury probability.
Swimming-pool operators must protect workers and pool users under general health and safety law.
Operators must complete a suitable and sufficient risk assessment and choose controls for the particular pool.
Lifeguard numbers and the need for constant supervision must be determined through risk assessment rather than a universal fixed number.
Where constant poolside supervision is not required, trained staff must be on call and able to respond immediately.
Pool rescue, CPR and first-aid competence are essential for staff assigned to emergency response.
Pool water treatment should follow recognised effective-management standards and suitable chemical controls.
Single sump outlets may need engineering changes such as a second outlet or pressure interlock to reduce suction-entrapment risk.
HSG179 provides updated guidance on pool operation, facilities, equipment, PPE, confined spaces and inflatable or raft use.
Pool controls depend on pool type, users, activities, supervision, water treatment, plant, outlets, occupancy and emergency response.
Swimming-pool evidence is facility-, activity- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level drowning or illness probability.
